decision.reason: Three blocking issues: the shipped default contradicts the documentation and defeats the PR's stated purpose; disabling the toggle takes down the entire v1alpha1 API for both RoleBasedGroup and RoleBasedGroupSet; and the new UPDATE rule denies three separate controllers including the HPA scale path.

inlineComments.body:
`values.yaml` ships `true`, while the README value table, the README prose ("By default … the chart ships in restricted mode for security") and the PR description ("default: `false`") all say `false`.

A default `helm template` grants all 8 legacy RBAC entries and emits no `--disable-v1alpha1-compatibility` argument at all, so as shipped the PR does not reduce RBAC for anyone who has not opted in, which is its stated purpose. As a control I rendered the same chart with the value explicitly `false` and got 0 legacy entries, so the conditional itself works and this is purely the default.

Which way to fix it depends on the other two blocking comments:

- if those are fixed in this PR, ship `false`. That is the end state, and earlier is better.
- if they are deferred, ship `true` and correct the three documents to match, then flip the default in the PR that fixes them.

I would suggest the second. Shipping `false` while those two stand turns a routine install into: every v1alpha1 write rejected, existing groups silently unreconciled, and HPA unable to scale them.

One knock-on to plan for either way. Renaming this key after release breaks users' values files, so it is cheapest to settle the name now, while nothing depends on it. See the separate note a couple of lines up.

This switch rejects a value that the conversion webhook writes into every object submitted via v1alpha1, including objects that never set a workload field. Three individually reasonable links compose into it:

1. `v1alpha1.RoleSpec.Workload` carries `+kubebuilder:default={apiVersion:"apps/v1", kind:"StatefulSet"}`. The API server applies that, so the field is never empty on a submitted object. I checked this read-only against a live k8s v1.36.1: a v1alpha1 RBG with no `workload` field comes back as `{"apiVersion":"apps/v1","kind":"StatefulSet"}`.
2. `convertRoleV1alpha1ToV2` copies it into the `role-workload-type` annotation, behind an `if … != ""` guard that the default renders permanently true.
3. This switch rejects exactly that value.

The distinction the validator needs is already written down, in `rolebasedgroup_conversion.go`:

> `// This annotation is for conversion compatibility only; …`
> `// New v1alpha2 RBGs should NOT set this annotation.`

So the intent exists, it just is not enforced here.

This seems worth deciding deliberately rather than inheriting. The PR describes itself as an interim RBAC reduction whose migration path is deferred to a follow-up, but as written it removes the API that the follow-up is meant to migrate.

The fix I would prefer is to reject only workload types explicitly chosen on the v1alpha2 API. `admission.Request.RequestKind` exposes the originally submitted version, so v1alpha1-submitted objects can be exempted. That does mean dropping from `CustomValidator` to a raw handler.

If that is out of scope for an interim PR, then at minimum the message should explain itself, and the README should say prominently that disabling the toggle currently disables v1alpha1 as a whole:

```
role "worker" uses workload type apps/v1/StatefulSet, which is deprecated and
disabled on this cluster (compatibility.v1alpha1.enabled=false).
Note: objects submitted via the v1alpha1 API always carry a workload type
(defaulted by the v1alpha1 schema), even if you never set one.
Fix: migrate the role to RoleInstanceSet, or set
     compatibility.v1alpha1.enabled=true.
```

That makes the failure explicable without preventing it.

Adding a validating webhook for RoleBasedGroupSet is the right call and closes a real gap from the previous round. Flagging one thing here so it does not get missed.

The v1alpha1 `rolebasedgroupsets` schema carries the same `{apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: StatefulSet}` default on `spec.template.roles[].workload`, and `rolebasedgroupset_conversion.go:37` routes through the same `convertRoleV1alpha1ToV2`. So the problem I described on `rolebasedgroup_validation.go` applies here too: with the toggle off, every v1alpha1 RoleBasedGroupSet is rejected wholesale, including ones whose template never mentioned a workload type.

A fix confined to the RoleBasedGroup validator, which is the natural thing to reach for, would leave this one broken.

Extending the webhook to `verbs=create;update` has a wider blast radius than it looks. Three separate controllers write the RoleBasedGroup main resource, and with the toggle off all three are denied for a group with a deprecated workload type. None of them sets a condition or event, and all three retry forever, so the only symptom is a controller quietly looping.

| Call site | What it writes | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `rolebasedgroup_controller.go:362` | `ensureDiscoveryConfigMode` patches an annotation onto the main resource on first reconcile | the group can never be reconciled at all |
| `rolebasedgroupset_controller.go:465` | RBGSet copies `groupTemplate.spec.roles` onto a child and `Update`s it | a pre-existing RBGSet error-loops forever; the sync is idempotent and still rejected |
| `rolebasedgroupscalingadapter_controller.go:511` | `updateRoleReplicas` sets `role.Replicas` and `Update`s, which is the HPA / scale path | HPA can no longer scale such a group. `retry.RetryOnConflict` only retries `Conflict`, so an admission `Forbidden` propagates straight out |

The RBGSet row is the previous round's RBGSet error-loop coming back. The new `RoleBasedGroupSetValidator` does correctly stop *new* RBGSets with a deprecated template, but objects already in the cluster are never re-validated, and the child-sync path is where the loop returns.

This population also is not exotic. The prescribed update path is uninstall-and-reinstall, and the CRDs are not Helm-managed (no `crds/` directory; they come from the `crd-upgrade` Job), so every pre-existing group survives and lands here.

A `RequestKind`-based exemption does not help with any of the three, incidentally: these writes come from the controllers using the typed v1alpha2 client, so they carry `RequestKind: v1alpha2`.

What I would suggest instead is validating the delta rather than the whole object. For each role in `new`, if its workload type is deprecated, allow it only if the role of the same name in `old` had the same deprecated type; reject newly introduced or changed types. That permits all three writes above, since the annotation patch changes no role, the RBGSet sync writes identical roles, and the scale path only changes `replicas`. It still blocks a user adding a new deprecated role. Requiring the type to be *unchanged*, rather than just "was deprecated before", also avoids grandfathering a swap between two deprecated types.

Whichever mechanism you pick, a group that cannot be reconciled should say so on itself rather than only in controller logs:

```
type=Degraded  reason=DeprecatedWorkloadTypeDisabled
message="role \"worker\" is backed by apps/v1/StatefulSet, which is disabled on
         this cluster; migrate to leaderWorkerPattern (see <link>)"
```

Raising this alongside the default value since both touch this key, and renaming it after release breaks users' values files, so now is the cheap moment.

Given the roadmap converges on RoleInstanceSet as the only supported workload type, this is a deprecation escape hatch rather than a compatibility mode. I would suggest `controller.deprecatedWorkloadTypes.enabled`:

- `deprecated` carries the Kubernetes lifecycle contract (warn, then default-off, then removed), which "compatibility" does not, so it tells users this is a one-way street;
- it fixes the scope. A pure-v1alpha2 user who picks a StatefulSet workload is rejected by this switch too, and "v1alpha1 compatibility" gives them no clue why;
- `WorkloadTypes` rather than `Workloads` matches the vocabulary already in the tree: the annotation is `role-workload-type`, the accessor is `GetWorkloadType()`, the constants are `DeploymentWorkloadType`, and the current error text says `workload type %q is not supported`.

One reason to avoid an ownership adjective like `native` or `builtin`: the types being removed are `Deployment` and `StatefulSet`, which are Kubernetes built-ins, plus `LeaderWorkerSet`, which is a CRD. The type being kept, `RoleInstanceSet`, is also a CRD. So no built-in/custom split separates those two sets, and both words read as *Kubernetes'* rather than *RBG's*. `deprecated` describes status instead, which stays accurate even for an actively developed external project like LWS.

Two things pair well with the rename whenever it lands. First, pass the value through instead of negating it: today `if not enabled` producing `--disable-…=true` takes two mental flips to read off a running pod, whereas `- --enable-deprecated-workload-types={{ $dwt.enabled | default false }}` takes none. Second, add the deprecation declaration, or a `deprecated…` key asserts something the project has not declared. There is no timeline in the README and the CRD carries no `deprecated` or `deprecationWarning`. That mechanism costs no code and warns on every v1alpha1 request including `get` and `list`. Since v1alpha1 is already `storage: false`, no object is persisted in that form, so eventually setting `served: false` removes an interface without touching data.

The rename does have to move as one change or the tree ends up with two vocabularies: 13 locations, including `cmd/rbgs/main.go` where the meaning inverts at each call site. Happy to post the full list if that helps.

notes: GitHub-facing comments should be written in English unless the publish gate is intentionally changed.
Phrase comments as reviewer feedback, not assistant narration.
Run a humanization pass before publishing and set --humanized only after that pass is complete.

summary.body:
Blocking on the following before merge:
- deploy/helm/rbgs/values.yaml:11 — The shipped default contradicts the documentation, so no RBAC is reduced by default
- api/workloads/v1alpha2/rolebasedgroup_validation.go:171 — Disabling the toggle disables the entire v1alpha1 API, not just deprecated workload types
- api/workloads/v1alpha2/rolebasedgroupset_admission.go:60 — The same chain reaches RoleBasedGroupSet, so the fix must cover both validators
- api/workloads/v1alpha2/rolebasedgroup_admission.go:87 — The new UPDATE rule denies three different controllers, including the HPA scale path
- deploy/helm/rbgs/values.yaml:9 — Settle the key name now, while nothing depends on it
